title: Synthesis of Hydrogels with Antifouling Properties As Membranes for Water Purification
protocol: Add 10.00 g of deionized water to a glass bottle with a magnetic stir bar.
Measure and transfer 2.00 g of SBMA to the glass bottle containing the water.
Stir the solution for 30 min until SBMA is completely dissolved.
In a separate bottle, add 20.00 g of PEGDA (Mn = 700 g/mol).
Add 20.0 mg of 1-hydroxycyclohexyl phenyl ketone to the PEGDA solution.
Let the solution stir for at least 30 min.
Transfer 8.00 g of the PEGDA-HCPK solution to the SBMA aqueous solution using a disposable pipette.
Stir continuously until the mixture is homogenous.
Add 6.00 g of deionized water and 4.00 g of ethanol to an amber glass bottle with a magnetic stir bar.
Stir the solution to allow thorough mixing.
Add 2.00 g of SBMA to the water/ethanol mixture.
Stir the solution until the SBMA is completely dissolved.
Transfer 8.00 g of the PEGDA-HCPK solution to the SBMA mixture using a pipette.
Stir thoroughly to mix the solution.
Place two spacers with known thicknesses on a clean quartz disc.
Transfer a small amount (~1.0 mL) of the prepolymer solution to the quartz disc using a disposable pipette.
Place another quartz disc on top of the liquid and ensure that there are no bubbles in the liquid film.
Irradiate the sample for 5 min using UV light with a wavelength of 254 nm.
Separate the polymer film from the quartz discs using a sharp blade.
Transfer the film to a DI water bath using tweezers.
Change the water twice during the first 24 h to remove solvent, unreacted monomer/crosslinker, and sol from the film.
Remove the film from the water bath and allow it to air dry for 24 h.
Place the film in a vacuum oven at 80 °C to dry overnight under vacuum.
Place a sheet of porous support onto a quartz disc.
Coat each side of the support twice with the prepolymer solution using a foam brush.
Place another quartz disc on top of the support.
Irradiate the sample for 5 min using UV light with a wavelength of 254 nm.
Immerse the assembly in a DI water bath for 5 min.
Remove the membrane using a sharp blade and tweezers.
Keep the membrane in DI water.
Change the water twice to remove impurities.
Allow the membrane to dry at ambient conditions for 24 h.
Dry the membrane in a vacuum oven overnight at 80 °C under vacuum.
Prepare a sample of the prepolymer solution for FTIR analysis.
Perform a background scan before scanning the sample.
Set the wavenumber range from 600 cm-1 to 4,500 cm-1 at a 4-cm-1 resolution.
Place the sample in the FTIR machine for analysis.
Remove the sample.
Clean the crystal and the tip with an appropriate solvent.
Repeat steps for porous support, prepolymer solution, dried freestanding films, and dried impregnated membranes.
Place a DSC pan and lid in a weighing balance.
Record their weight.
Place a small amount of sample (5-10 mg) inside the pan.
Close the pan with the lid.
Weigh the pan containing the sample.
Calculate the weight of the sample from the difference in weights between the occupied and unoccupied pans.
Hermetically seal the sample inside the pan with a press.
Place the sealed pan in the DSC cell alongside the inert reference.
Enter the weight of the unoccupied pan and lid along with the sample weight into the program.
Scan using DSC from -80 °C to 160 °C at a heating rate of 10 °C/min.
Repeat the DSC experiments for different samples as outlined above.
Cut a rectangular strip of the membrane sample (approximately 30 mm by 6 mm).
Soak the membrane in DI water for 10 minutes and then dry it for 5 minutes.
Place the dried sample on the sample holder.
Submerge the sample holder in an environmental chamber containing DI water.
Dispense approximately 1 µL of n-decane onto the membrane surface using a microliter syringe with a stainless steel needle.
Leave the setup undisturbed for 2 minutes to stabilize droplets.
Use image analysis software to measure and determine contact angles of the samples from the dispensed droplets on the membrane surface.
Take the average of contact angle values obtained across various droplets.
Use a hammer-driven hole punch with an appropriate diameter to cut coupons of freestanding films and impregnated membranes.
Place a prepared coupon on the porous support inside a dead end filtration cell.
Place the O-ring on top of the sample.
Screw the two halves of the permeation cell together.
Add approximately 50 mL of DI water to the permeation cell.
Screw on the cap and place the permeation cell on a magnetic stirrer.
Set the stirring rate between 300 and 900 rpm.
Place a covered beaker on a balance to collect the permeate water.
Tare the balance.
Open the valve on the gas cylinder.
Turn the pressure regulator valve clockwise until the desired pressure is reached (45 psig for freestanding films and 35 psig for impregnated membranes).
Open the release valve to deliver the pressure to the permeation cell.
Use a BSA solution containing 0.5 g/L BSA in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) with pH = 7.4.
Repeat steps 4.4.5 - 4.4.10 to determine the water flux in the presence of BSA.
Calculate the BSA rejection rate using the equation RBSA = [(CF - CP) / CF] × 100%,
where RBSA is the BSA rejection rate of the membrane (%),
CP is the concentration of BSA in the permeate (g/L),
and CF is the concentration of BSA in the feed (g/L).
Determine the concentration of BSA via UV spectroscopy.
